posts.text:
The race for the position of next United Nations Secretary-General is tightening, with the UAE’s Minister of State and former permanent representative to the UN Lana Nusseibeh emerging as one of the frontrunners after her candidacy was announced late last month.

The UN Security Council is currently under pressure to break the deadlock as a new Secretary-General has to be in place by January 1st 2027 as António Guterres's term expires on New Year’s Eve.

The field has narrowed to 8 candidates:

🇦🇷 Rafael Mariano Grossi – Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency

🇨🇷 Rebeca Grynspan – Secretary-General of UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD)

🇪🇨 María Fernanda Espinosa – Former President of the UN General Assembly

🇪🇨 Ivonne A-Baki – Diplomat and former ambassador

🇬🇾 Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett – Guyana's Permanent Representative to the UN 
🇺🇬 Olara Otunnu – Former UN Under-Secretary-General

🇦🇪 Lana Nusseibeh – UAE Minister of State and former UN Ambassador 

🇹🇷 Feridun Sinirlioğlu – Former Turkish Foreign Minister 

Lana Nusseibeh is considered a strong candidate who knows the system as she has chaired the Security Council twice  during her 11 years as the UAE’s ambassador to the UN.

During her time in the Security Council, she successfully drafted and led negotiations on Resolution 2681 (adopted in April 2023 with Japan regarding Afghan women's rights) and Resolution 2720 (adopted in December 2023 regarding humanitarian aid to Gaza).

She has also served as UN General Assembly Vice-President in the past, building strong relations in another important UN body.

In December 2023, two months into the Israel-Hamas  war, she led a Security Council delegation to the Rafah crossing — the visit credited with paving the way for Resolution 2720 and the delivery of humanitarian aid. 

Her opponents and rivals in Latin America claim that she can’t become the next Secretary General as she’s not from Latin America and the post must, by regional rotation praxis, be passed on to a Latin American.

In reality, regional rotation is custom, not a Charter requirement and has recently been opposed by 2 out of the 5 permanent members of the security council.

Whoever finally takes the positions as the UN next Secretary General will have their hands full as the world is the most unstable it has been since the Second World War.

🚨🇨🇴 A suspected car bomb blew up outside a state government headquarters in Colombia

The blast reportedly hit the Meta governor's building in downtown Villavicencio tonight, wrecking nearby shops and offices.

Early counts range from two injured to 12, and no group has claimed it.

It comes days after the military bombed FARC dissidents in that same state, and eight days after another car bomb hit a toll station on the highway to Bogotá. 

Up north in Cúcuta, guerrilla drones aimed at a police station damaged more than 60 homes and injured a couple and their baby, in what's being called the first drone attack on a major Colombian city.

Colombia's president answered tonight by saying there will be no talks with "narco-terrorism."

That leaves force as his only move, against groups that just showed they can reach a state capital with a car bomb and a border city from the air.

Source: El Tiempo, Infobae, @TabzLIVE on TG / Writer: Daniel

🚨 INSANE LEVEL OF MANIPULATION IN THE CRYPTO MARKET.

Bitcoin and Ethereum pumped after the Jensen Huang news, only to crash even harder within hours.

And look at how traders got wiped out on BOTH sides.

• First 30 minutes: $375 MILLION in shorts liquidated.

• Bitcoin then crashed 7.8%, while Ethereum crashed 9.5%, wiping out the entire pump.

• As prices crashed, another $240 MILLION in longs were liquidated.

That's $615 MILLION in total liquidations in just a few hours.

And all this happened despite other markets pumping massively, with no negative news to explain the crypto selloff.

Crypto traders are getting absolutely crushed while the rest of the market rallies.
